{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "0xB10C",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "provided Guix build hashes"
    },
    {
      "login": "davidgumberg",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "ACKed with size benchmark measurements and Guix hashes"
    },
    {
      "login": "sedited",
      "stance": "question",
      "note": "provided Guix build hashes and asked about PR status/drafting"
    },
    {
      "login": "Sjors",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "demonstrated that --icf=safe without -faddrsig folds address-significant functions on Darwin"
    },
    {
      "login": "theuni",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "concerned that Guix-only linker flags would hide linker issues from developers; resolved by moving flags to general build"
    },
    {
      "login": "hebasto",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Concept ACK on ICF, but objected that -faddrsig is required for Darwin and noted safe shadows safe_thunks in probe order"
    },
    {
      "login": "151henry151",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "not an ACK as-is; proved address-significant function folding on Darwin LLD 19 and analyzed probe order"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:4461546707",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Without -faddrsig, --icf=safe on Mach-O targets behaves like --icf=all, breaking function pointer uniqueness and folding address-significant functions.",
      "quote": "My LLM friend thinks that `--icf=safe` is not actually safe, because without an address-significance table (`-faddrsig`) it's equivalent to `--icf=all`.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "demonstrated with repro examples by multiple reviewers that Mach-O LLD requires -faddrsig to avoid unsafe folding",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4461591584",
        "c:5238854292"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4935892434",
      "status_by_quote": "The issue applies to both safe_thunks and safe, so still relevant as of 24ad7419dea40e647b10791105a0659df143e014."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:4499825348",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "Enabling ICF only for Guix builds hides potential linker issues from developers building locally.",
      "quote": "I worry that if any linker tricks like this cause any trouble, we'd only see it in guix binaries.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "resolved by moving flags to general build",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4544457401",
        "c:4875779934"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:4875779934",
      "status_by_quote": "I've pulled this back out of REDUCE_EXPORTS, into the general flags."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3652466874",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "The linker flag probe order appends --icf=safe after --icf=safe_thunks, which causes safe to override safe_thunks on toolchains supporting both.",
      "quote": "This prioritizes `--icf=safe` over `--icf=safe_thunks` on the linker command line. However, shouldn't it be the other way around, since `safe_thunks` does not rely on the address-significance table?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [
        "c:5136916557"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5136916557",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "On the pinned Guix toolchain, LLD 19 Mach-O folds address-taken functions unless -faddrsig is passed across core and depends, corrupting dispatch tables and function identity.",
      "quote": "Not an ACK in its current shape — on the pinned Guix toolchain, `--icf=safe` behaves like `--icf=all` for the Darwin release binaries. Adding `-faddrsig` fixes that and keeps most of the size win",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5763613739",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Should this PR be drafted or what is its current status?",
      "quote": "Should this be drafted, or what is the current status of this?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author replied stating upstream docs landed and will push shortly",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:7227307164"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:7227307164",
      "status_by_quote": "This landed. Will push here again shortly."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:4446990079",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "nice win in binary sizes, with Guix size benchmarks showing ~5% savings across Darwin binaries",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "both",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "r:4781720529",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "on using the \"Identical Code Folding\" linker feature where possible",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": []
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Added question from sedited regarding draft status, answered by fanquake stating a push is forthcoming.",
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "push fix adding -faddrsig / probe order adjustments as promised",
      "id": "c:7227307164"
    }
  ]
}
